planting.note: Plant bare-root bushes in autumn or early spring while dormant, in cool-summer regions where this late-flowering Scottish selection performs best.

directions: Ben Dorain is a Scottish Crop Research Institute release from the Ben Alder breeding line, flowering roughly a week later than 'Ben Lomond' and ripening correspondingly later, which can help dodge frost damage to blossom. It carries good resistance to mildew and leaf spot, though like most of the Ben series it remains susceptible to gall mite and the reversion virus the mites spread, so source certified virus-free stock. Fruit hangs well on the bush without splitting, giving growers a wider picking window, and yields are strong under cool, moist Atlantic-influenced climates similar to its native Scotland. Prune in winter by cutting out roughly a third of the oldest wood each year to keep the bush renewing itself from the base.

planting.note: Plant bare-root bushes in autumn or early spring while dormant; self-fertile, so a single bush can crop alone, but it also makes an excellent pollinizer for neighboring black currants.

directions: Andega was bred by INRA in France from a 'Noir de Bourgogne' x 'Öjebyn' cross and released in the late 1980s, combining the rich, aromatic flavor of its Burgundy parent with improved disease tolerance. The bush grows with medium vigor and carries long, well-filled strigs of black fruit with a pinkish bloom, ripening over a compact window in early to midsummer. It shows good resistance to powdery mildew and, being self-fertile and heavy-blooming, is often planted specifically to boost pollination and set in mixed currant plantings. Give it an annual thinning of old wood in winter to keep young, productive shoots coming from the crown.
